item.title: reports: per-currency totals
item.brief: In the reports Python repo, read the CSV on stdin per the shared contract and total per account and currency. Output header `account,currency,total_cents`, rows sorted by account then currency. Input without a currency column counts as USD. A malformed currency code prints an error to stderr and exits 2. Add unittest tests for: new CSV with currency, old CSV without currency column, sort order, malformed code exit 2. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing. Keep functions under 60 lines and validate at the input boundary. Update the README to describe the output. Commit the change in this repo only.

state.summary:
Implemented per-account, per-currency totals in the reports repo. reports.py now reads an optional currency column (absent means USD), groups totals by (account, currency), and prints `account,currency,total_cents` sorted by account then currency. A malformed currency code (not exactly three uppercase A-Z) prints an error naming the line to stderr and exits 2 with no stdout. Added 4 unittest tests (new CSV with currency, old CSV without the column, sort order, malformed code exit 2 across five bad codes) and updated README.md. `python3 -m unittest` passes: 5 tests OK on commit adef1e7. Before, the currency column was ignored (EUR and USD summed together) and malformed codes were accepted. Review agt_01M7W5ZJQEEXC77TMY6T48BC99 passed the head with no blocking findings. Non-blocking follow-ups, not fixed: header matching is case-sensitive, so a `Currency` header is silently read as USD; a short row reports "malformed currency code None"; the README does not flag the header change as breaking for position-based consumers. Risk is high because the output shape changes for every caller. Nothing is running; no services were started. Only the commit is on the branch; not pushed.

pr.body: Approach: reports.py detects the currency column from the CSV header; rows without it are USD. Totals are keyed by (account, currency) and rendered sorted. A currency that is not exactly three uppercase ASCII letters raises CurrencyError, caught in main(), which prints the line number to stderr and returns 2 before any output. Files: reports.py, test_reports.py (4 new tests), README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 5 tests OK on adef1e7 (tree 1bf00cf0). Review: agt_01M7W5ZJQEEXC77TMY6T48BC99 passed the whole change with no blocking findings. Follow-ups, not fixed: header matching is case-sensitive; short-row error text says None; README does not flag the header change as breaking. Assumptions: a present currency column with an empty value is malformed (exit 2).
pr.summary: reports now totals per account and currency. now: optional currency column (default USD), malformed code exits 2. before: currency ignored, EUR and USD summed together, malformed codes accepted. now: header account,currency,total_cents.
pr.title: reports: total per account and currency

risk.why: Output header changes from account,total_cents to account,currency,total_cents, and legacy input also gains a USD column, so the CLI output shape changes for every caller; position-based consumers would read the currency code where they expect the total. Rubric: CLI change that breaks callers. No in-repo consumer exists (reviewer checked git grep). Tests cover the changed behaviour and pass.

item.title: ledger: currency column
item.brief: In the ledger Rust repo, add the optional fourth currency column per the shared contract: default USD when missing, validate exactly three uppercase ASCII letters, output header `date,account,amount_cents,currency` with currency on every row. Malformed currency: error naming the line number to stderr, exit 2; other input errors keep exit 1. Add tests for the new behaviour (default, explicit code, malformed code, line number in error, exit codes). Keep `cargo test` passing. Keep functions under 60 lines and validate at the input boundary. Update the README to describe the format. Commit the change in this repo only.

state.summary:
Added the optional fourth currency column to the ledger CLI in commit 2366cf640dc89772e73f5a922c94546a9740f5e3 on archon/pr901vnw-ledger-currency-column (based on main ebcd6da). The fourth TSV column is optional and defaults to USD; a present code must be exactly three uppercase ASCII letters. Output header is now `date,account,amount_cents,currency`, with currency on every row. A malformed currency prints `line N: bad currency ...` to stderr and exits 2; other input errors still exit 1. pr.body: Approach: Entry gets a currency field. parse_line accepts 3 or 4 TSV fields; the 4th is validated by is_currency (exactly three ASCII uppercase letters, trimmed like other fields) and defaults to USD. ParseError distinguishes Input (exit 1) from Currency (exit 2) via exit_code(); main.rs uses it for the exit status. to_csv_row emits currency and asserts the invariant with debug_assert. Key files: src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, tests/ledger.rs, tests/cli.rs (new, runs the built binary), README.md. Checks: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test (14 passed). Assumptions: whitespace around the currency code is trimmed, as other fields are; an empty 4th column is a currency error, not a field-count error. Downstream: the reports tool must accept the new 4-column header (sibling item).
pr.summary: Ledger export gains an optional currency column (default USD) and validates it as three uppercase letters. Before: 3 columns, no currency, exit 1 for all errors. Now: 4-column output with currency on every row; malformed currency exits 2, other errors exit 1.
pr.title: ledger: add currency column

risk.why: Changes the CLI output format (new header and a currency column on every row) and the exit code for malformed currency (2). Callers that parse the 3-column output or check exit 1 are affected, so the rubric's CLI-breaking-change clause applies. Behaviour is covered by unit and CLI tests and matches the contract. The reviewer rated it medium on compatibility grounds; high was kept because it breaks callers and the rubric says when in doubt, go higher.
